Action Plan:
1. Empirical treatment for suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis: prescribe Trimethoprim (oral, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days; exact strength not documented).  
2. Symptomatic relief: advise regular paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), adequate oral hydration, and cranberry juice as adjunct.  
3. Pregnancy exclusion: patient to perform a home urine pregnancy test today; instructed to contact clinic with the result.  
4. Safety-netting: patient to seek immediate review if abdominal pain worsens, develops vomiting, objective fever, or other new symptoms; otherwise scheduled telephone review in 3 days to assess response.  
5. Investigations discussed (urine dipstick/culture, serum β-hCG) but deferred at patient’s request; will be arranged if no improvement or test results concerning.  
6. Electronic prescription to patient’s nominated pharmacy today.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 2-day history of constant, gradually worsening burning pain below the umbilicus.  
• Associated symptoms: ↑ urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine, mild nausea, subjective fever/diaphoresis. No dysuria, vomiting, diarrhea, flank pain, respiratory or cardiac symptoms.  
• Onset & course: Gradual onset, worsening over 48 h; pain localized, not radiating.  
• Past medical/surgical history: None. No previous similar episodes.  
• Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted 1 yr ago; no regular oral medications.  
• Allergies: Not discussed/documented.  
• Gynecologic/sexual: Sexually active with single partner (last intercourse 4 days ago); LMP ≈2 weeks ago; uses Implanon only; prior STI screen negative 6 months ago.  
• Social: Lives in share-house with two roommates; accountant; non-smoker; social alcohol.

Objective:
• No in-person examination performed (telephone consult).  
• No vital signs obtained.  
• No laboratory or imaging results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Suprapubic abdominal pain / suspected acute cystitis  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute cystitis (High likelihood ‑ DDx).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute appendicitis (Medium, DDx) – pain pattern and constitutional symptoms overlap; no RLQ localization yet.  
     • Ectopic pregnancy (Medium–Low, DDx) – reproductive age; needs exclusion.  
     • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Low–Medium, DDx) – systemic symptoms but no discharge/dyspareunia.  
     • Ureteric/renal stone (Low, DDx) – hematuria present but pain not colicky, no flank radiation.  
   – Investigations planned: Urine dipstick & culture; defer today, arrange if no clinical improvement.  
   – Treatment: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (strength/route not documented); hydration, cranberry juice, paracetamol for pain.  
   – Referrals: None at this stage.

2. Possible pregnancy  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pregnancy status unknown; needs exclusion.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Ectopic pregnancy (Medium–Low, DDx) if positive test; normal intra-uterine pregnancy.  
   – Investigations planned: Home urine pregnancy test today; consider serum β-hCG and pelvic ultrasound if positive or symptoms escalate.  
   – Treatment: None until results available.  
   – Referrals: Early pregnancy assessment service if positive or ectopic suspected.

3. Follow-up / monitoring  
   – Assessment: Need to monitor response to antibiotics and evolving abdominal pain.  
   – Investigations planned: As above if no improvement.  
   – Treatment: None additional.  
   – Referrals: Urgent review or emergency services if red-flag symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing data: Allergies, current medication doses, vital signs, physical examination findings, urinalysis, and pregnancy test result.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient name recorded as “Tim” initially then “Kim” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor name inconsistency and occasional filler words but overall understandable.
